_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Model-Based Engineering Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analysis Profile (SysML Version)
summary: Prescribes the failure modes, effects, and criticality analysis (FMECA) data elements and design views to be captured in a digital system model, including a SysML profile example, so FMECA data can be interactively delivered to the program office.
use_relationship:
The failure modes, effects, and criticality analysis (FMECA) is a foundational reliability and maintainability (R&M) engineering design activity implemented during the design and development of a product or system. The FMECA identifies potential failure modes for independent single-item or functional failures, as well as the resulting effects on mission success, performance, safety, reliability, and maintainability. The FMECA, when performed early in the design process, allows for the implementation of appropriate corrective actions needed to eliminate Severity I and II failure modes or control risks associated with each remaining failure mode. Controlling critical failures can improve operational readiness and reduce life cycle cost.

This Systems Modeling Language (SysML) profile supports the move from static document delivery in this DID to interactive model delivery of FMECA data to allow FMECA data to be dynamically provided to the program office and other users allowing quicker engagement, decreasing design cycle times, and increasing design influence. This enables reliability and other engineering functions to continuously exchange information to identify and eliminate or control failure modes throughout a system's life cycle and apply the information as a basis for detecting and isolating faults, determining operator and maintainer actions, and identifying test requirements. The MBE approach allows engineers to interrogate the design to address the design views in Table 1. Figure 1 is an example implementation using a SysML profile.

This profile contains standard data elements needed to generate MBE FMECA design views as required by the specific and discrete tasks described in the solicitation (contract statement of work). The selection of required design views should be tailored appropriately by selecting only those views in Table 1 needed for the program.

This Data Item Description (DID) contains the format, content, and intended use information for the data product resulting from the work task described in the contract SOW.

To be considered compliant, with this DID, it is encouraged to use SysML to add and manage the data elements listed in this DID and report the design views with the properties described in this DID. This does not mean that it is required to use the accompanying MBE FMECA Profile; however, it can be used as an out-of-the-box tool to allow a team to easily be compliant with this DID.

This DID is intended to prescribe the FMECA data elements that need to be captured for a system and define the Design Views, or the format that the data should be reported back in. The SysML Profile is intended to be an out of the box SysML tool to assist in this DID compliance by:
- Allowing the capture of the prescribed data elements through the use of a FMECA stereotype and tags
- Allowing the compilation of those data elements into the required design views by using generic tables

While the provided MBSE FMECA Profile will assist in compliance, with this DID, it is not required to be used. The MBSE Team is welcome to modify the provided FMECA Profile or create their own, provided that it captures the DID Data Elements and Design Views.

Further instructions for how to implement, model, and customize the accompanying SysML Profile can be found in the model itself.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

children.title: Integrated Process
children.content: The FMECA process shall be integrated within the digital system model. The Digital System Model shall represent the functions described in the system specification requirements as elements of the model.

children.title: Model Interrogation
children.content: The MBE approach shall provide methods and access for the government to interrogate the digital system model to view data elements and their relationships per the pre-defined design views in Table 1. The interrogation shall have the ability to query, filter, or sort by:

children.title: Design View or Design View Subcategory
Metachain
children.content: Combination of data elements not defined in Table 1 Design Views.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: The FMECA shall be delivered in the native file format(s) of the modeling tool(s) or developed directly in the Integrated Digital Data Environment (IDDE) as identified in the Contractor's Systems Engineering Management Plan. The FMECA shall include documentation regarding necessary software tool(s) configurations, access types (e.g., readonly or write access), dashboards, views, data integrations, data flows, reporting mechanisms outside of dashboards (e.g., report building tools), security, size, and configuration management details.

preparation_instructions.title: Content
preparation_instructions.content: The design views and associated data elements provided in Table 1, document the relationship of the FMECA to the SysML model, digital engineering artifacts, and R&M engineering analyses, as required by the contract statement of work.

children.title: The FMECA shall state how it is
children.content: incorporated into the Digital System Model.

children.title: The FMECA shall state how flows
children.content: are analyzed.

children.title: Functional Traceability
children.content: The Digital System Model shall contain a traceability matrix demonstrating that all functions requested in the specification requirements are covered.

children.title: Flows
children.content: The FMECA data shall be linked to model elements of the Digital System Model representing power flows between LRUs; fluid flows (e.g., fuel, cooling) between LRUs; internal communications flows between software components; external communications flows between the system and other systems or actors in the system context; and other signal flows such as relay closures, synchronization clock signals, and similar flows between line replaceable units and/or software components.

children.title: A1 - Identification Number
children.content: Serial number, Logistics Control Number (LCN) or other reference designation identification number is assigned for traceability purposes.

children.title: A2 - Item Identification Nomenclature
children.content: The name or nomenclature of the item or system function being analyzed for failure mode and effects.

children.title: A3 - Function
children.content: A concise statement of the performance required by the function of the item including any performance standards.

children.title: A4 - Function Failure Description
children.content: Ways an item can either partially (with upper and/or lower performance limits) or totally fail to perform its functions.

children.title: Incorrect Disposition
children.content: The item is not in a state that bears the desired function when the function is called.

children.title: Interrupted Change of Disposition
children.content: The item exited from state such that it can no longer physically complete the desired function.

children.title: Performance
children.content: The item was in and remained in proper state and physically performed the desired function, but some quality of the function's execution did not meet performance.

children.title: B1 - Failure Modes
children.content: From the data entity perspective, the description of the relational difference between the desired condition and the predicted failed condition pointing from desired to fail. For incorrect disposition type failures, this will point between two operational states. For interrupted disposition type failures, this will point from operational to failed states. For performance failures, this will point from predicted (failed) performance to performance requirement (e.g., open, short, low torque, loss of power, etc.).

children.title: B2 - Failure Causes
children.content: Identification and description of the root cause(s) of the failure modes. The model should include process models that lead to a failure mode. Root cause is the point of deviation that leads to the failure mode (e.g., failure mechanism such as fracture, fatigue, corrosion, spalling, etc.).

children.title: B3 - Operational/Mission Phase
children.content: Description of the required higher-level process within which the failure may occur. Performed for all mission profile(s), under worst-case conditions.

children.title: B4 - Operational Mode/State
children.content: Description of the operational state of an item defined by a set of functions.

children.title: B5 - Failure Effects
children.content: Performance effects that identify the impact of a failure mode on the operation and function of a linked item.

children.title: C1 - Failure Signatures
children.content: Unique set of characteristics that will support detection and isolation of the failure.

children.title: C2 - Failure Detection Method
children.content: Description of the methods by which occurrence of the failure mode is detected by the operator or maintainer at the system level.

children.title: C3 - Isolation Procedure
children.content: Description of the most direct procedure that allows a maintainer to isolate the malfunction or failure. Describes the method by which ambiguities are resolved when more than one failure mode causes the same failure indication. Identifies to what indenture level failures can be isolated by the use of BIT features and indicate when ancillary test equipment will be required for failure isolation.

children.title: D1 - Compensating Provisions (Design / Operator)
children.content: Compensating provisions, either design provisions or operator actions, that circumvent or mitigate the effect of the failure.

children.title: D2 - Protection
children.content: Protective or preventative measures to prevent the failure effect from occurring.

children.title: D3 - Mitigation
children.content: Mitigation of the end effect.

children.title: D4 - Protective Comments
children.content: Explanation of the protective measure or documentation of uncertainty.

children.title: D5 - Implemented By
children.content: The system feature, component, or instructions that allow the operator to implement the compensating provisions.

children.title: E1 - Intermediate Effects
children.content: Identification of each of the effects (secondary failures) as the primary failure propagates through the system until its end effect.

children.title: E2 - Intermediate Causes
children.content: The failure causes associated with each of the intermediate effects.

children.title: E3 - Intermediate Items
children.content: Identification of each item along the failure's path of propagation through the system until its end effect.

children.title: E4 - Intermediate Detections
children.content: List of all detection mechanisms other than the primary and end effect detections along the propagation path.

children.title: E5 - Intermediate Protections
children.content: List of all protection measures other than the primary and end effect protection measures along the propagation path.

children.title: E6 - Intermediate Mitigations
children.content: List of all mitigations other than the primary and end effect mitigations along the propagation path.

children.title: E7 - Intermediate Comments
children.content: Explanation or uncertainties on the intermediate detections, mitigations, or protections.

children.title: F1 - End Effects
children.content: End effects used to evaluate and identify the total performance effect of a failure on the mission and the surrounding environment.

children.title: F2 - End Cause
children.content: The cause of the failure at the end item.

children.title: F3 - End Item
children.content: The item at which the failure propagation terminates.

children.title: G1 - Severity Classification
children.content: Categories (I-IV) assigned to each failure mode, without considering compensating provisions, according to the failure effect at the uppermost system. The severity classification categories are:

children.title: Category I - Catastrophic
children.content: A failure that may cause death or system loss (i.e., aircraft, tank, missile, ship)

children.title: Category II - Critical
children.content: A failure that may cause severe injury, major property damage, or major system damage that will result in mission loss.

children.title: Category III - Marginal
children.content: A failure that may cause minor injury, minor property damage, or minor system damage that will result in delay or loss of availability or mission degradation.

children.title: Category IV - Minor
children.content: A failure not serious enough to cause injury, property damage, or system damage, but will result in unscheduled maintenance or repair.

children.title: G2 - Severity Comment
children.content: Explanation or uncertainty in determining the severity.

children.title: G3 - Unmitigated Severity Classification
children.content: Categories (I-IV) assigned to each failure mode, without the consideration of any compensating provisions, according to the failure effect at the uppermost system.

children.title: H1 - Basic Corrective Maintenance Actions
children.content: The basic actions taken by the maintainer to correct the failure (e.g., remove and replace LRU)

children.title: H2 - Basic Preventative Maintenance Actions
children.content: The basic actions taken by the maintainer to prevent the failure (e.g., oil change).

children.title: I1 - Remarks
children.content: Any pertinent remarks or contractor's rationale pertaining to and clarifying any other columns or recommendations for design improvements.

children.title: J1 - Failure Probability
children.content: Assessment of failure modes in terms of probability of occurrence (Levels A-E):

children.title: Level A - Frequent
children.content: High probability of occurrence, which may be defined as a single failure mode probability greater than or equal to 10^-1 of the overall probability of failure during the operating time interval.

children.title: Level B - Reasonably probable
children.content: Reasonable probability of occurrence, which may be defined as a single failure mode probability of occurrence that is more than 10^-2 but less than 10^-1 of the overall probability of failure during the item operating time.

children.title: Level C - Occasional
children.content: Occasional probability of occurrence, which may be defined as a single failure mode probability of occurrence that is more than 10^-3 but less than 10^-2 of the overall probability of failure during the item operating time.

children.title: Level D - Remote
children.content: Remote probability of occurrence, which may be defined as a single failure mode probability of occurrence that is more than 10^-6 but less than 10^-3 of the overall probability of failure during the item operating time.

children.title: Level E - Extremely unlikely
children.content: Extremely unlikely, which may be defined as a single failure mode probability of occurrence that is less than 10^-6 of the overall probability of failure during the item operating time.

children.title: J2 - Failure Rate Data Source
children.content: When failure rate data are to be used in the calculation of criticality numbers (item W), the data source of the failure rates used in each calculation. When a failure probability is listed, the remaining items J3-J6 are not required.

children.title: J3 - Failure Effect Probability (Beta)
children.content: The conditional probability that the failure effect will result in the identified criticality classification, given that the failure mode occurs. The values represent the analyst's judgment as to the conditional probability the loss will occur and should be quantified in accordance with the following:

children.title: J4 - Failure Mode Ratio (Alpha)
children.content: The fraction of the part failure rate related to the particular failure mode under consideration.

children.title: J5 - Failure Rate (Lambda)
children.content: The failure rate from the appropriate reliability prediction.

children.title: J6 - Operating Time (t)
children.content: The operating time of the item per mission derived from the government-approved operational concept or System Requirements Specifications.

children.title: J7 - Failure Mode Criticality Number [cm = (Beta Alpha Lambda t)]
children.content: A relative measure of consequence of a failure mode and its frequency of occurrence.

children.title: J8 - Item Criticality Number [cr = sum of (Beta Alpha Lambda t)]
children.content: A relative measure of consequence of an item failure and its frequency of occurrence.

children.title: K1 - FMEA Prevention Action
children.content: Description of how a potential cause resulting in a given failure mode is mitigated using existing and planned activities.

children.title: K2 - FMEA Detection Action
children.content: The simulations or tests available to detect that the potential failure mode during the manufacturing or production process.

children.title: K3 - Responsible Organization
children.content: Organization responsible for corrective action.

children.title: K4 - Target Completion Date
children.content: Date corrective action is due.

children.title: K5 - Status
children.content: Current status of corrective action development.

children.title: K6 - Actions Taken with Reference to Evidence
children.content: Description of the corrective action and evidence that it was effective.

children.title: Schema
children.content: Example of how to apply data element stereotypes to capture system FMECA data (Figure 1).
